title: AutoSum and the status bar total

screens.prompt: In B7, total the stock column A2:A6 with AutoSum.

hints.syntax: AutoSum writes =SUM( for you; typed out it is =SUM(B2:B8).
hints.func-sum: The seven amounts are added by SUM over their own column, which is what the AutoSum button inserts.
hints.require-ref: Sum the amounts in B2:B8; adding seven typed numbers leaves the character of the range behind.
hints.value: Add the seven amounts from the top row down to Bank fees, and stop before the typed total.
hints.error: A total divided by zero returns #DIV/0!, which is what an empty divisor cell produces.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so the total never computes
the stale typed total in B9 is added on top, so every expense counts twice
the bank fees in B8 are left out of the range
copies the stale figure instead of adding the column
the amounts typed into the formula, so a corrected expense never reaches the total
a total divided by zero returns #DIV/0!
answers how many expenses there are, not what they add up to

docs.explain: The AutoSum button guesses a range from the numbers above or beside the active cell and inserts =SUM( with that range already selected. Here the run of numbers stops at B8, because B9 holds a figure somebody typed by hand months ago. Selecting the whole column instead of the seven amounts is the classic way to double a total: 476 becomes 896. The status bar is the check — highlight B2:B8 and it shows Sum 476 before you write anything. AutoSum is a guess, not a proof: it looks for the nearest run of numbers and stops where the run stops, so the honest habit is to press it, look at which cells got highlighted, and fix the range before pressing Enter again on the total.

errors.text: The total was divided by a blank cell, often an average column whose count is not filled in yet.
The function name was typed by hand as =SUMM(, which the sheet cannot recognise at all.

docs.atWork: A monthly expense sheet where one stale hand-typed total sits under the live figures.
docs.outcome: Total a run of expenses and spot the stale figure that would double it.
